messages:
Aisha: Heads-up — after rolling exp-kernel-bias-042 to canary, small-seq p95 jumped ~30% on g4 instances. Not seeing obvious GPU util change, but launch wait stacks are up in pprof.
Marco: Repro steps?
Aisha: Dumped a pprof flame: a lot of time in kernel_selector::choose() + stream.launch overheads. Flame attached: https://internal/pprofs/exp-kernel-bias-042 (note: link is placeholder)
Priya: Did the autotuner change heuristic to prefer the fused-attn kernel for seq<=32? That one has higher kernel launch overhead but better per-token throughput. If scheduler groups many tiny requests into narrow continuous batches we might be losing to launch overhead.
Marco: Yes — last commit made fused-attn preferred on Ampere for short seqs because microbenchmarks favored it at high batch sizes. But we didn't simulate high microburst arrival patterns.
Jon: Also saw KV cache warmup behavior: cached requests get routed to the legacy fast-launch path during warmup, so the autotuner flips affinity back-and-forth. We probably have a bimodal workload: cold requests that can amortize launch, and hot cached hits that need low launch latency.
Aisha: Here's a short trace I recorded (trimmed):
```
req 1: seq=12 cached=false -> kernel=fused-attn (launch 120us)
req 2: seq=8  cached=true  -> kernel=legacy (launch 30us)
scheduler groups -> batch split -> extra launch cost 220us
```
Priya: That matches my local sim. Two things to try: 1) Add a launch-cost penalty into the autotuner objective (bias against kernels with high per-launch cost when observed inter-arrival < X ms). 2) Add scheduler hysteresis so we avoid switching kernel affinity inside a short window.
Marco: +1. We should also instrument the scheduler to expose batch-size distribution and inter-arrival histograms to the console dashboard for this customer. Right now we only get avg batch size.
Jon: For immediate mitigation we can set exp flag kernel_selector.force_affinity=legacy for canary and roll back the heuristic change. ops-bot: Canary rollback scheduled by release-bot at 21:05 UTC if approved.
Aisha: I ran a microbenchmark script that toggles the fused kernel off with the same traffic profile — p95 drops back near baseline. I'll attach numbers to the issue.
Priya: Long-term: autotuner objective should be multi-term: tokens/sec, launch-count-weighted-latency, and cache-hit routing stability. We should feed in per-model seqlen distribution as a prior.
Marco: Agreed. I'll open a PR with: 1) add launch_cost term, 2) sticky-affinity window (configurable), 3) instrumentation for batch histograms. Assign to me + Priya for review. Ticket: INF-2197.
Aisha: Filing infra ticket and adding perf traces to INF-2197. Thanks — let's keep the canary paused until we have the sticky-affinity toggle.
ops-bot: deploy-canary exp-kernel-bias-042 status: PAUSED by Aisha at 2170001299 :pause_button:
Jon: Quick note — we should run a small A/B with real KV-hit rates (10%/50%/90%) to validate. I'll queue that in staging tomorrow.
Aisha: Sounds good. If anyone wants my pprof export I put it in /artifacts/pprof/2170001234-exp-kernel-bias-042.pb.gz
Marco: OK, will start the PR and add the new metrics to the console. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:"
